articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表期間中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027シーズン最初の代表戦ウィーク中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースと更新情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

articles.headline: Mike LaFleur's coaching roots fast track to NFL
articles.description: The Shanahan-LaFleur dynamic spreads to Arizona, where new head coach Mike has taken the reins in the desert.
articles.headlineJa: マイク・ラフルーアのコーチとしてのルーツがNFLでの急速なキャリア躍進につながる
articles.descriptionJa: シャナハンとラフルーアの系譜がアリゾナにも拡大。新ヘッドコーチのマイクが砂漠の地でチームの指揮権を握りました。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Arizona -- Mike LaFleur's career is about to come full circle on Sunday.

Twelve years ago, as a 27-year-old, LaFleur's first NFL season was spent on the banks of Lake Erie as an offensive intern for the Cleveland Browns under the direction of a young, up-and-coming offensive coordinator named Kyle Shanahan.

Until then, LaFleur had spent his coaching career at small colleges such Division III Elmhurst, Division II J Joseph's and Division I FCS Davidson, watching his older brother, Matt, make the jump to the NFL in 2008 and engrain himself with a group of young, nascent coaches who would go on to become friends and a coaching "crew," as one of them described it, that currently holds six of the league's 32 head-coaching jobs.

In Week 1, that "crew", which includes Rams head coach Sean McVay, Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh, Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur and Shanahan, the San Francisco 49ers head coach, watched as Mike LaFleur walked the sidelines as a head coach for the first time, getting a win in his debut. And on Sunday, they'll all have an eye on his first game as a head coach against his NFL sherpa, Shanahan, when the Cardinals visit the 49ers (4:05 p.m. ET, Fox). Mike LaFleur was Shanahan's pass game coordinator and wide receivers coach from 2017 to 2020.

The sentimentality of the moment Sunday has lost its shine after LaFleur faced Shanahan six times during three seasons as the Rams' offensive coordinator, but this one will, eventually, mean something.

"When you're in the moment, you're in the moment, you're not thinking about that stuff," LaFleur said. "I'm excited to see him before the game, obviously, say what's up, but then it's on and that's how they're going to feel and that's how we feel.

"And I'm sure when all is said and done next February and we get to see each other in the offseason, we'll talk about it. But I mean, this is the Niners versus the Cardinals."

In LaFleur, who followed Shanahan from Cleveland to the Atlanta Falcons and then to the 49ers -- seven straight seasons in all -- Shanahan saw someone who was "as good as any of those other guys" that Shanahan had on his staff.

That's saying something coming from Shanahan.

Seven of his former assistants, starting from his time as the Houston Texans' offensive coordinator in 2008 to his time as the 49ers head coach, have gone on to become NFL head coaches. And it's quite a group: McVay, Matt LaFleur, Saleh, Hafley, former Dolphins head coach and current Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans and, now, Mike LaFleur.

"I've had a couple of these guys and Mike's right there with all those dudes in terms of he's very smart, he knows the game," Shanahan said. "There's lots of coaches who can do some good stuff, but you always know guys in your building who see it a little bit better than most people, and Mike's one of those guys."

What can we expect in Jets coach Aaron Glenn's return to Ford Field? And will we see a bunch of points in a showdown between the Ravens and Cowboys?

articles.headline: Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga demand FIFA reform amid Gianni Infantino re-election bid
articles.description: The top leagues in England, Italy, Germany and Spain have issued a joint-statement demanding governance reform at FIFA, amid Gianni Infantino's bid to be re-elected as president in 2027.
articles.headlineJa: インファンティーノ氏の再選出馬を受け、プレミア、ラ・リーガ、セリエA、ブンデスがFIFAの改革を要求
articles.descriptionJa: 2027年の会長再選を目指すジャンニ・インファンティーノ氏の動きを受け、イングランド、イタリア、ドイツ、スペインのトップリーグがFIFAのガバナンス改革を求める共同声明を発表した。
articles.body:
Four of Europe's biggest leagues -- the Premier League, LaLiga, the Bundesliga and Serie A -- have called for reform at FIFA in the wake of Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has vowed to stand for re-election as FIFA president next year despite the uproar caused by the proposal, labelled "FIFA Forward Enterprise," which has now been withdrawn due to the scale of opposition to the idea.

In a joint statement issued on Friday, the four leagues said Infantino had "actively promoted abusive initiatives rather than protecting football from them" and called for fundamental reform at world football's governing body.

As well as the sell-off plan, this summer's World Cup saw a number of controversies involving FIFA and Infantino, including the decision to overturn the red card awarded to United States men's national team forward Folarin Balogun.

"In recent years, football's historic foundations have been threatened by a fundamental governance problem," the statement said. "The FIFA President has actively promoted abusive initiatives rather than protecting football from them.

"And although football stakeholders ultimately succeeded in having the FIFA Forward Enterprise [FFE] project withdrawn, the conditions that gave rise to it remain in place.

"The FIFA President has now acknowledged the need for reform, but considering superficial procedural changes in the wake of the FFE episode is not enough; a profound governance reform is essential to re-establish clear constitutional limits within FIFA and ensure, among other things, that individual disciplinary matters remain unequivocally protected from any political interference."

The four leagues went on to accuse FIFA of "relentless expansionism," saying the body "unilaterally makes far-reaching decisions that directly affect us, such as expanding the International Match Calendar."

They went on to call for "a new governance structure" for FIFA, which would include the establishment of "a permanent body representing key stakeholders, including national associations, leagues, clubs, and players from both men's and women's football," which would "receive full information regarding new initiatives and play a meaningful role in FIFA's decision-making process."

The leagues also called for FIFA's plans to be "based on a clearly defined rationale, supporting data, and an independent assessment, all published before any decision is adopted."

articles.headline: Seahawks encouraged by Jadarian Price leading RB room
articles.description: Seattle's running back committee has no touchdowns through two weeks, but there's another opportunity this week at Commanders.
articles.headlineJa: ジャダリアン・プライスがRB陣を牽引、シーホークスに期待感
articles.descriptionJa: シアトルのランニングバック陣は2週を終えてタッチダウンがないが、今週のコマンダーズ戦で新たな好機を迎える。
articles.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Three things were apparent with running back Jadarian Price while watching the Seattle Seahawks' first-round pick during training camp.

One, he has plenty of speed, even if not the same fifth gear as the guy he's replacing (Kenneth Walker III). Two, he's better in the passing game than his limited college production as a pass catcher would suggest. And three, while he will be the Seahawks' RB1, he has plenty of company in their backfield -- especially once Zach Charbonnet returns.

So, much of what we've learned about Price during Seattle's 2-0 start has merely been confirmation of what was already assumed.

After not playing a down in the preseason, the Seahawks limited Price's workload to 24 snaps in Week 1. He gained 58 yards on 12 touches against the New England Patriots. That included a 13-yard run on the first play of his NFL career. In a Week 2 win over the Arizona Cardinals, Price played 24 snaps and touched the ball 14 times for 60 yards. That included a 25-yard run that set up their second touchdown, as well as an 11-yard run when the Seahawks went right back to the rookie after he lost a fumble on the previous drive.

"I've thought he's done well," offensive coordinator Brian Fleury said Thursday. "We gave him a little more last week and he showed up, had a couple explosive runs that he was able to break and run through contact. So I'm happy with the development we've seen, and I think it'll just continue to show itself."

Price was sidelined against the Cardinals after hurting his chest/shoulder late in the third quarter. However, he took part in the first two practices of this week as a limited participant and appears to have a good chance of playing Sunday against the Washington Commanders (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

Through two games, Price leads Seattle's backfield in snaps with 47 and in touches with 26. George Holani has looked like the clear RB2 since the start of the offseason program, and he has out-snapped Emanuel Wilson 38 to 31. But Wilson has 23 touches compared to Holani's 13.

However, that trio is still looking for its first touchdown. Wilson couldn't find the end zone on three consecutive carries from inside the 5-yard line late in the second quarter against Arizona, leading to a turnover on downs. But he came through on the Seahawks' final possession to help close it out.

With Price out and Holani briefly joining him on the sideline, Wilson carried the ball 10 times for 48 yards on a 16-play touchdown drive that took more than 10 minutes off the clock. He finished with 92 yards on 21 attempts after playing just three snaps in the opener.

"It's the things that we saw him do throughout training camp before he had that minor setback," coach Mike Macdonald said of Wilson, who was sidelined for part of the summer with a hamstring injury after signing a one-year deal with Seattle in March. articles.headline: The Rams are better when both RBs get the ball
articles.description: Through two weeks, Williams and Corum have nearly split the carries exactly.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズは2人のRBが共にボールを持つ時により好調となる
articles.descriptionJa: 開幕2週間で、ウィリアムズとコーラムはキャリー数をほぼ半々に分け合っている。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The night the Los Angeles Rams drafted running back Blake Corum in the third round in 2024, coach Sean McVay said Corum reminded him of another running back.

He was referring to a running back already on the roster: Kyren Williams.

At the time, Williams had finished up his second NFL season and was firmly the Rams' RB1. In 12 games that season, Williams ran for 1,144 yards and 12 touchdowns on 228 carries and had 32 catches for 206 yards and three touchdowns.

But while Williams and Corum are similar, McVay said he believes the team is better when both are getting the ball. McVay said Williams and Corum are "similar in stature, but I also think they bring some unique things."

"It's like a pitcher changing up his pitches," McVay said.

Through two weeks, Williams and Corum have nearly split the carries exactly. Williams has 23 carries for 126 yards and a touchdown, while Corum has 22 carries for 133 yards. Last season, it was closer to a 65%-35% split in Williams' favor. 

"We look at it like we have two great backs," McVay said. "Those guys being able to spell each other, I think, is when we're at our best."

Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said Corum and Williams are "as alike of two running backs" as he's played with during his 18-year NFL career, saying, "I feel like those two guys, we feel like we can call any play in our playbook at any time with either of those guys in there and feel really confident about it."

"I could imagine as a playcaller that's a really comforting feeling knowing that whoever's out there, everything is up and we're ready to rock and roll," Stafford said. "They give us that great flexibility on offense."

The pair know they'll be alternating drives, Williams said. Corum said there wasn't really a conversation this offseason in which McVay or running backs coach Ron Gould told them they'd be splitting carries, but "more so just building trust."

"It's a long season and so we never really had a conversation [of] how we're going to split carries," Corum said. "It's more so of 'let's keep you guys fresh. You guys play really well off each other. I trust both of you guys and let's go from there.'"

While Corum earned McVay's trust last season, he said his goal during the offseason was to work on being more explosive.

Last year, Corum averaged 2.1 yards before contact per carry, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That was the highest mark of any running back with at least 100 carries. In two games this season, he has found even more space before contact, gaining 3.1 yards before contact on average.

"I feel like when I hit the hole, I'm hitting it pretty fast," Corum said. "I trust myself. Now it's just a sense of making more people miss, breaking that 60-yarder. Every time I get the ball, I try to be as explosive as I can."

articles.headline: Why are the Jaguars using CB/WR Travis Hunter sparingly?
articles.description: The highly anticipated two-way player is playing half of defensive snaps and has barely been seen on offense. But coach Liam Coen said it's by design.
articles.headlineJa: ジャガーズはなぜCB/WRトラビス・ハンターを控えめに起用しているのか？
articles.descriptionJa: 大きな注目を集める二刀流選手は守備スナップの半数に出場しているものの、攻撃ではほとんど起用されていない。しかしリアム・コーエンHCは意図的な計画だと述べている。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Travis Hunter has had a relatively quiet start to his second season with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The 2025 No. 2 overall pick started both games at cornerback but is being rotated in and out during games. He has been on the field for only 57.4% of the team's defensive snaps. On offense, he has played 11 snaps and touched the ball twice for a total of 11 yards.

That might raise some concern that the Jaguars are either misusing Hunter -- a player general manager James Gladstone said would "alter the trajectory of the sport" -- or he is struggling. However, the organization is not concerned. They say Hunter's decreased role, especially as part of the cornerback rotation, is by design.

"We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," coach Liam Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

"But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

Hunter doesn't seem to have a problem with the way he's being used.

"Coaches tell me what I've got to do. I just follow the plan and follow their lead," Hunter said in the locker room after the Jaguars' 20-13 loss to Denver last Sunday. "My job is to play no matter when they put me out there so that's what I try to do."

Hunter is rotating with Montaric Brown and Jarrian Jones at outside cornerback. Two of those three are on the field on each drive. Hunter has played 62 defensive snaps in the Jaguars' two games. Brown has played the most defensive snaps (85, 78.7%) of the trio, per ESPN Research. Jones has played 72 (66.7%).

Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said that's not a knock on Hunter but more because they like the way Brown -- whom the Jaguars signed to a three-year, $31.8 million contract extension in the spring -- and Jones performed in the offseason and training camp.

Through two games, Jones is allowing a 37.5% completion rate as the nearest defender, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Brown is at 66.7% and Hunter at 75%. Hunter and Jones each have a pass breakup while Brown leads the trio with six tackles (Hunter has five and Jones has one).

"We feel like we had a bunch of good players there, guys that do a good job and have worked their tail off," Campanile said. "We feel good about all those guys. So keeping them fresh and rotating them all, that's kind of been the philosophy behind [the rotation]."

What is a little surprising is that the Jaguars haven't played Hunter much on offense -- just four snaps against Cleveland and seven against Denver -- considering he played 67% of the team's offensive snaps in seven games last season before his season-ending knee injury. articles.headline: Texans face troubling trend when they play without Nico Collins
articles.description: Houston has seen a dip in scoring, and quarterback C.J. Stroud has seen his QBR decrease when targeting others.
articles.headlineJa: テキサンズ、ニコ・コリンズ不在時に直面する懸念される傾向
articles.descriptionJa: ヒューストンは得点が減少しており、クォーターバックのC.J.ストラウドも他のレシーバーを狙った際のQBRが低下している。
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- The absence of Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins has created a trend for the Houston Texans.

In the last three games, including the playoffs, that Collins has missed because of injury, Houston's ability to score has been a mixed bag. Even though quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards last week, the Texans (0-2) lost 20-6 to the Cincinnati Bengals without Collins (hamstring), and Houston has averaged 16 points in that span.

Coach DeMeco Ryans understands how vital their No. 1 wideout is to the success of the offense, but he's challenging others to step up.

"Everyone knows Nico is one of the top receivers in the league," Ryans said. "A lot of guys have to step up to fill that void left by Nico. The bottom line is everybody is here, everybody gets paid to go make plays. We have to find a way to do that. We definitely, of course, miss Nico. When you have such an explosive threat in Nico, it's hard on a defense."

He also didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday as Houston prepared to travel to face the winless Indianapolis Colts on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS). That usually is an indication in Houston that he won't play as the Texans tend to be cautious with soft tissue injuries.

Collins rested in the Week 18 finale against the Colts last season, and Stroud and other starters didn't play in the second half of the 38-30 win. But in the last three games when Collins was injured and didn't play, Stroud averaged 294 passing yards per game and threw three touchdowns with five interceptions -- four coming in their playoff loss to the New England Patriots.

Houston has struggled to find a receiver to step up in Collins' absence. In those three games, no receiver has eclipsed 70 receiving yards, and only three have gone over 55 in Xavier Hutchinson (69) against the San Francisco 49ers in 2025, Jaylin Noel in that same game (63), and Jayden Higgins (59) -- who is expected to miss the season -- against the Patriots. Being without Higgins and Collins means the Texans are down their top two wide receivers.

In last week's loss to the Bengals, Houston failed to score a touchdown. Tight end Dalton Schultz had 140 yards on 12 catches, but when it came time to beat man coverage, the wideouts struggled -- as Stroud went 8-of-20 for 102 yards against that coverage in Week 2. Kayshon Boutte (acquired in a trade before the season to help soften the blow after the loss of Higgins) and Hutchinson led the receiving corps with 37 yards a piece. 

One way to help overcome the loss of Collins, who had 7 receptions for 75 yards and a touchdown in the opener against the Buffalo Bills, is an effective running game to help keep them out of third-and-long situations where teams tend to play more man coverage.

Houston's 3.7 yards per carry ranks better than only nine teams, and the Colts have played man coverage on 50% of the snaps (third most this season) against third-and-7 or longer.

articles.headline: United Strand fan: Ruben Amorim told me 'sorry about that'
articles.description: The Manchester United fan who has vowed to cut his hair only when the club win five Premier League games in a row has received an apology from former boss Ruben Amorim.
articles.headlineJa: 「髪を切らない」ユナイテッドサポーター、ルーベン・アモリム前監督から「申し訳ない」と謝罪を受ける
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドがプレミアリーグで5連勝するまで髪を切らないと誓っているサポーターが、ルーベン・アモリム前監督から謝罪を受けた。
articles.body:
The Manchester United fan who has vowed to cut his hair only when the club win five Premier League games in a row has said he received an apology from former boss Ruben Amorim.

Frank Ilett, who goes by United Strand, achieved virality on social media for his hair-growing stunt. His last haircut came on Oct. 5 2024, with United failing to win five in a row in that period.

Amorim's tenure as United boss fell between this period and he had a chance interaction with Ilett at the Portugal Football Summit this week.

Ilett posted a picture with the now-AC Milan manager on his 1.5 million-strong Instagram account with the caption: "Great to meet Ruben Amorim at the @portugalfootballsummit.

"He saw me, pointed to my hair and said 'sorry about that!'

"Still have love for him!"

Amorim was sacked by United in January of this year, just 14 months into his three-year contract. Michael Carrick has become the latest United manager following Amorim and Erik ten Hag who has so far proved unable to win five matches in a row and earn Ilett a trim.

United nearly achieved the feat early in Carrick's tenure after wins over Manchester City, Arsenal, Fulham and Tottenham. However, a 1-1 draw against West Ham in the fifth game saw Illet return to square one.

Far from five successive wins, United have picked up just seven points from a possible 15 this season. They needed a late Matheus Cunha to secure a draw against Fulham in the final game before the international break.

Through his haircut challenge, Ilett is raising money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

articles.headline: European Golden Shoe: Who's leading Raphinha, Mbappé, Haaland in race for top goal award?
articles.description: Raphinha may have started the season on fire, but there's a little-known striker who is ahead of the Barça star in the race for the European Golden Shoe.
articles.headlineJa: 欧州ゴールデンシュー：最多得点賞争いでハフィーニャ、ムバッペ、ハーランドらを抑えて首位に立っているのは誰か？
articles.descriptionJa: ハフィーニャは今シーズン素晴らしいスタートを切ったかもしれないが、欧州ゴールデンシューを巡るレースでは、このバルサのスター選手を抑えて首位を走るあまり知られていないストライカーが存在する。
articles.body:
Having made a fantastic start to the 2026-27 campaign, Raphinha has -- perhaps against the odds -- emerged as one of the most fearsome strikers in Europe this season after moving in from the wing to play in a central role for Barcelona.

In fact, Barça's club captain and makeshift center forward is firmly among the favorites to win the 2026-27 European Golden Shoe, which is awarded to the continent's top marksman every season.

Occupying the spot formerly occupied by two-time Golden Shoe winner Robert Lewandowski, who left Barça to join MLS side Chicago Fire over the summer, Raphinha has already racked up 12 goals in just seven LaLiga games including back-to-back hat tricks in his past two outings, scored just four days apart.

It might be early days, but the Brazil international has so far comfortably outscored high-profile rivals such as Erling Haaland (five goals in five games), Kylian Mbappé (seven in seven) and last season's Golden Shoe winner Harry Kane (three goals in four games) at the first international break of the season.

That said, there is currently one player above Raphinha in the race to claim the 2026-27 Golden Shoe award.

Who is leading the European Golden Shoe race?

The one player across all of Europe's top divisions who is beating Raphinha in the scramble for the 2026-27 Golden Shoe is Joseph Ede Oloko. The striker has been scoring goals at a phenomenal rate for in Latvia's top flight, the Virslīga, firstly on loan at Tukums 2000 and then back at parent club FK Liepāja.

Oloko has netted 25 goals in 27 league games to top the scoring charts in Latvia. The 25-year-old also has five more games to add to his season tally with the league set to conclude in early November.

His goal-scoring exploits this year have earned him a first senior callup for Benin in this international break. Following Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Burkina Faso and Mauritania, Oloko's first involvement with the national team will conclude with a trip to Buenos Aires for a friendly that will serve as Lionel Messi's farewell match for Argentina.

While he may have scored more than double the amount of goals, Oloko is only a hair's breadth ahead of Raphinha in the Golden Shoe ranking thanks to the points-based coefficient system that is used to calculate the leaderboard. In fact, he's leading the way by just a single point.
